articles.title: VC firm Bessemer now has another $5.75B to invest in (what else?) AI
articles.full_text:
Bessemer Venture Partners announced on Wednesday that it has raised $5.75 billion across two new funds to accelerate its investment across all parts of the AI stack. The firm, which has backed companies such as Anthropic, Cognition, Legora, Perplexity, Ramp, Shopify, and Waymo, dedicated $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and the remaining $4 billion for growth startups.

Bessemer has been well-known as a leading VC in the SaaS era, with a particular knack for picking enterprise winners, like Box, Docusign, and Gainsight. Since 2022, it has invested in more than 260 AI-native companies. So far, the firm has invested $3 billion into AI-related startups, it says, including those focused on compute, infrastructure, foundation models, dev tools, app-layer startups, and agentic tech.

Now, Bessemer positions all things AI as the opportunity of a lifetime — a common sentiment, until the next big trendy tech revolution comes around, of course.

“AI-native companies are scaling faster than any category of technology we’ve backed before,” Bessemer Partner Byron Deeter said in the company’s funding announcement. VC firms also need to keep increasing their war chests, Deeter told Bloomberg, because companies staying private longer has become “a permanent structural shift.”
articles.summary:
Bessemer Venture Partners has raised $5.75 billion across two new funds to expand its investments across the entire AI stack, reinforcing its shift from a SaaS-focused legacy to an AI-first strategy.

  • Core Event: The firm announced $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and $4 billion for growth-stage startups, targeting opportunities from compute and infrastructure to foundation models, developer tools, and application-layer AI.
  • Background: Bessemer built its reputation as a leading SaaS investor with wins like Box, DocuSign, and Gainsight. Since 2022, it has backed more than 260 AI-native companies and deployed roughly $3 billion into AI-related startups, including Anthropic, Cognition, Perplexity, and Waymo.
  • Impact: The raise signals continued investor conviction that AI-native companies are scaling faster than previous tech categories, while also reflecting a broader trend of VC firms amassing larger funds as startups stay private longer.
  • Outlook: Bessemer is positioning AI as the defining opportunity of the current cycle, though the firm's ability to replicate its SaaS-era success will depend on picking winners across an increasingly crowded and capital-intensive AI landscape.
